BLOCKING: the repair can't pass on the two Windows probe runners at any point before quest 0.14.1 is latest, so the release sequence deadlocks.
- setup-quest tries `npm install -g "@opum-ai/quest@<declared>"` (action.yml:39). On failure its source fallback refuses Windows by design (action.yml:69-71: "does not support Windows runners"). The probe matrix includes win32-x64 and win32-arm64 (release.yml:988, `runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}`).
- Measured on npm: quest stages its candidate as the LAUNCHER `@opum-ai/quest@X-rc.1` under release-candidate, with platform packages at exact X. The launcher at exact X is published only at the latest promotion: 0.13.0-rc.1 at 12:31Z, 0.13.0 at 14:53Z on 2026-10-07. So `@opum-ai/quest@0.14.1` doesn't exist until quest moves to latest.
- Article 3.5 moves latest only after BOTH families are staged and qualified, and lore's staging Release needs this probe green on Windows. Lore can't stage until quest is latest, and quest can't go latest until lore is staged. The v0.14.1 dry run would fail its two Windows arms by construction, the same shape as run 39347496150.
Fix, lore-cli's to implement: setup-quest's npm path, when exact `@opum-ai/quest@<declared>` doesn't install, installs `@opum-ai/quest@release-candidate` ONLY if that dist-tag's version has the declared base (`<declared>-rc.N`). Its existing assertion that the installed quest reports CLAUDE.md's declared version stays the guard. Prove it both ways in its own test: a declared version with only an rc staged installs the rc, and an rc of a different base is refused. Then the sequence is: quest stages rc, then lore's dry run and staging, then e2e, then latest, with no deadlock. Put that order in LCLI-714's notes.

UNMEASURED, for the dry run to show, not blocking: the previous-release arm now runs lore 0.13.0 with quest 0.14.1 on PATH. My earlier local run of that arm had quest 0.13.0 on PATH, so I never measured it against a newer quest. If lore 0.13.0's pair lock refuses quest 0.14.1 BEFORE it loads the agent profile, its output won't carry `Unrecognized key: "targets"` and the absent arm fails for the wrong reason. The v0.14.1 dry run (publish:false) measures it on Linux. If it fails that way, it comes back to me before any change.

Everything else is sound:
- The derive step reads `Quest CLI 0.14.1` from CLAUDE.md:268 under `shell: bash`, so it works on Windows too.
- The ci.yml/release.yml same-commit test with its mutation control is the right way to stop the two pins drifting apart.

Nothing lands until the fix is in and I confirm the delta.

RELEASE ORDER AFTER THE DEC-182 FIX, 2026-10-20. Nothing in steps 1-3 requires the other side to be latest.

MEASURED, for the lead's question about what an rc launcher reports. `npm view @opum-ai/quest@release-candidate version` = `0.13.0-rc.1`. Installed into a temp prefix and run: the launcher package.json reads `0.13.0-rc.1`, `node_modules/.bin/quest` is a symlink to `@opum-ai/quest/bin/quest.cjs`, the only platform package present is `@opum-ai/quest-darwin-arm64@0.13.0`, and `quest --version` prints `0.13.0` — the BASE version, because the platform binary answers it. Consequences, both favourable: setup-quest's existing assertion (`reported` must equal the declared version) needs no relaxation and stays the guard, and lore's full-string pair lock (src/adapters/quest.ts:53, `reported === VERSION`) accepts a staged rc without change. The rc form never reaches either comparison.

FIX IMPLEMENTED, .github/actions/setup-quest/action.yml, npm step: when the exact `@opum-ai/quest@<declared>` install fails, read npm's `release-candidate` dist-tag once (stdout parsed for a version line, stderr reported to the log so a failed read is not silent), and install it ONLY when that version's base equals the declared version; otherwise fall through to the existing source build, which still refuses Windows loudly. Both directions proven by EXECUTING the action's own run block under bash against a stub npm, in test/ci-workflow.test.ts (posix-only, for the documented reason): exact-available installs exactly; only-rc-staged installs the rc; a different-base rc is refused and falls back; an unreadable tag falls back and prints what it read. Two mutations of the check were run: disabling the staged branch reddened exactly the rc-install test, and dropping the base comparison reddened exactly the different-base test.

STILL OPEN, unmeasured and not this change: the probe's PREVIOUS-release arm now runs lore 0.13.0 with quest 0.14.1 on PATH. If lore 0.13.0's pair lock refuses quest 0.14.1 before it loads the agent profile, its output will not carry `Unrecognized key: "targets"` and that arm fails for the wrong reason. The v0.14.1 dry run measures it on Linux, and if it fails that way it goes back to opum-doc before any change.
